traders.name: RiskOff
traders.style: Cash guardian. Flip to BND when SPY < 200-day; equity (VOO) only while SPY > 200-day; high skip rate.

traders.name: Swing

coresat.name: Core-satellite with confirmation-gated semis
coresat.thesis: Keep 70-80% in a broad US core (VOO/VTI) and use a 15-25% satellite (QQQ, SMH, SOXX, VGT, XLK) for tech/semis upside. The core is sized by structure; the satellite only grows after price confirmation, not on the first dip.
coresat.regimeFit: Risk-on: core 75-80%, satellite up to 25%. Elevated vol (VIX > 22) or SPY < 200d: core 80%, satellite ≤ 15%, no satellite adds.
entryRules: Top up the core when it is below 72% of NAV and cash > $10.
Add to a satellite ETF only if it closes above its 50d SMA for 2+ sessions after a ≥ 3% drawdown day, and not within 1 session of CPI/FOMC.
Satellite adds are ≤ 5% of NAV per ticket.
exitRules: Trim any satellite holding above 22% NAV back to 18%.
Trim the whole satellite to ≤ 15% if SPY closes below its 200d SMA.
sizingRules: Max 2 orders per day; minimum ticket $5; cash buffer ≥ $5.
riskRules: Satellite and core overlap (both cap-weighted tech-heavy), so count AI exposure across both.
Avoid adding duration-sensitive tech right before CPI when the 10y > 5.3%.

mega.name: Equal-weight mega-cap, phased rebalance
mega.thesis: Own the six mega-cap platforms (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, NVDA) at roughly equal weight so no single AI or consumer story dominates. Rebalance mechanically but phase the adds, so that a single-day narrative shock (like Oct 8) is not bought all at once.

entryRules: Buy the most underweight name whose RSI14 < 65 and that is not > 8% above its 50d SMA.
When several names are underweight, add the least-extended first; stage the rest across sessions/days.
Avoid buying a name on the day it is the epicenter of negative news; re-check next session.
exitRules: Trim any name above the 25% hard cap back to ~25% at the next open session.
Soft-trim a name above 22% when RSI14 > 70.
No stop-losses on individual names (diversified long-only sleeve); risk is controlled by caps.

Max 3 orders per day; minimum ticket $5.

Earnings: no adds to a name within 2 sessions before its earnings date.

riskoff.name: 200-day guardian with CPI-gated duration
riskoff.thesis: Protect capital first. SPY vs its 200-day SMA is the master switch: below it, hold only BND and cash; above it, equity (VOO) is allowed up to 40% but only on pullback entries. Duration (BND) is added in steps when yields are high and the next inflation print has cleared.
riskoff.regimeFit: SPY < 200d: 0% equity, BND ≤ 70%, rest cash. SPY > 200d: optional VOO ≤ 40% on pullbacks (VOO ≥ 3% below its 20-day high), BND 40-60%, cash ≥ 25%.
entryRules: BND add (~$10) only when its RSI14 < 40 AND the most recent CPI/FOMC event has passed without the 10y closing above 5.35%.
VOO only when SPY > 200d AND VOO is ≥ 3% below its 20-day high.
exitRules: Flip: if SPY closes below its 200d SMA, sell all VOO at the next open session (and keep BND).
Never sell BND to chase equities.
sizingRules: Max 1 order per day; minimum ticket $5.
Cash ≥ 25% of NAV at all times.
riskRules: Stocks and yields are strongly negatively correlated right now, so BND is not a reliable equity hedge. Size duration modestly.
High skip rate is expected; "hold" is the default output.

swing.name: High-bar trend pullback + concentration discipline
swing.thesis: Take 3-15 day swings only in liquid tech names/ETFs that are in an uptrend (above 50d and 200d) and pulling back on no thesis damage. Act once per day at the pre-close batch. Cutting concentration and cap breaches takes priority over new entries.
swing.regimeFit: Risk-on, VIX < 20: entries allowed. Narrative shock in the target group (e.g., AI hardware Oct 8): no entries for ≥ 3 sessions; trims allowed. VIX > 25 or SPY < 200d: exits only.
entryRules: Pullback: 3-8% off the 10-day high with RSI14 between 40 and 55.
No entry within 1 session of CPI/FOMC or the name's earnings; confidence ≥ 0.65.
exitRules: Trim any position above the 25% NAV cap at the next pre-close batch.
Exit on a close below the 50d SMA, or after 15 sessions, or at +10% from entry (half) with a trailing 50d for the rest.
sizingRules: New entries ≤ 15% NAV; hard cap 25% NAV per name.
Max 1 order per day (pre-close only); minimum ticket $5.
riskRules: No bottom-fishing below the 200d (e.g., AVGO after Oct 8).
Count NVDA + SMH + TSM + AVGO together as one AI-hardware bet; combined ≤ 45% NAV.

value.name: Global-cap Bogle DCA
value.thesis: Buy and hold low-cost total-market index funds, adding on a schedule and never selling to time the market. Use each scheduled buy to steer toward a global market-cap mix (US ~60-65%, ex-US ~35-40%), because US cap-weighted indexes are now unusually concentrated in a few AI megacaps.
value.regimeFit: Same behavior in every regime: scheduled DCA. High rates or volatility only change where the next dollar goes (the most underweight fund), never whether to sell.
entryRules: One DCA ticket per trading day at the midday session, into the most underweight fund vs target (VTI 45%, VOO 15%, VXUS 35%, cash 5%).
Skip the ticket only if it would push cash below $10.
exitRules: No discretionary sells. Rebalancing sells need an explicit --override-reason and only when a fund drifts > 15 points from target.
sizingRules: Ticket ≈ $10 (or 50% of excess cash above $10, whichever is smaller).
Max 1 order per day; minimum ticket $5.
riskRules: Behavioral rule: news, rates and AI headlines are logged as context but cannot trigger sells.
Fractional ETF fills are modeled; real brokers may require whole shares.

ideas.thesis: NVDA is 35.7% of NAV, over Swing's 25% cap after a large gain vs cost. Oct 8 broke the AI-hardware tape (-2.94%, SOX -3.4%) on a demand-narrative reset plus vendor-financing worries. Trimming to cap at the pre-close batch is risk discipline.

ideas.whyRejected: Not a swing setup: below 50d and 200d, 25% off its high, and the $50B OpenAI financing makes it the epicenter. Strong 10-Q fundamentals (+85% revenue) do not override a broken trend for a 3-15 day hold.
Already 29.6% of NAV (over cap), and a one-day -2.8% after +80% YTD is not a high-bar pullback entry.

decision.summary: No new entries. At pre-close, trim NVDA to the 25% cap, and trim SMH too if it closes below its 50-day. Hold the ~35% cash for a post-CPI setup.
decision.reasoning: Swing only acts at the pre-close batch and only on high-bar setups. The research shows a sentiment break in AI hardware (OpenAI ~$50B vs ~$68B run-rate, AVGO arranging $50B+ of buyer financing) on top of 5%+ yields and hike odds, while money rotated into equal-weight and energy. That is a reason to cut concentration, not to bottom-fish. NVDA and SMH are both over the 25% cap, so the only trade I plan is the NVDA trim, with an SMH trim conditional on a 50-day break. Confidence 0.68 meets Swing's 0.65 bar for the trim.

plan.trigger: Always today (cap breach), unless NVDA is up >3% on the day (then reassess)
Only if SMH < 50d SMA (~$577) near the close

risks: A sharp AI rebound (the "accounting not demand" read) would make the trim look early.
Swing allows one order per day, so the SMH conditional competes with NVDA; NVDA has priority.
Pre-close quotes can lag ~15 min on the free feed; slippage is 5 bps plus the SEC fee on sells.

decision.summary: Do one DCA ticket of about $10 into VXUS at midday to start the international sleeve, keep about $13 cash, and sell nothing.
decision.reasoning: Value is a buy-and-hold DCA sleeve, not a timing sleeve. The research did not change the rule (keep buying broad index funds) but did change where the next dollar goes. US cap-weighted indexes are now unusually concentrated (record 42% in ten AI names; equal weight lagging by the widest margin in 24 years), and the sleeve has zero ex-US. VXUS is the only fund in the allowlist below its 50-day. Rates at 5.2% and a likely December hike are a reason to keep a cash buffer, not a reason to sell index funds. I will buy at midday after the open settles, since Value only does one order a day.

plan.trigger: Always (scheduled DCA), unless the sleeve cash would drop below $10

risks: A stronger dollar on higher US rates can weigh on VXUS in USD terms.
Small tickets: fractional ETF fills are modeled; real brokers may not allow fractional ETF shares (Schwab Stock Slices covers S&P 500 stocks only).
CPI on Oct 14 could move everything; DCA accepts that.
